data.narrative: The student consistently used hypothesis-first debugging on both bugs: they separated symptom from cause, proposed specific tests, and ruled out the wrong layer quickly. They also showed strong systems thinking by recognizing that pagination failures under concurrency were not just math errors, but consistency and ordering problems that needed a deterministic sort key.

dimension_scores.observation: They formed specific, falsifiable hypotheses before changing anything and used cheap tests to eliminate wrong causes quickly.
dimension_scores.evidence: They contrasted app logic vs process lifecycle for Bug 1, then chose unstable ordering first for Bug 2 because it was the cheaper, higher-signal check.

dimension_scores.observation: Logs were not the main focus in this module, so there was limited direct evidence of reading a log narrative.
dimension_scores.evidence: The work centered on command output and reproduction rather than reconstructing a multi-line log story.

dimension_scores.observation: They used minimal reproduction well: in-process handler execution for Bug 1 and repeat-query/concurrent-insert reasoning for Bug 2.
dimension_scores.evidence: They said the in-process redirect test returned 307 and that rerunning the same pagination query under concurrent inserts exposed the moving-goalpost problem.

dimension_scores.observation: There was no live stakeholder pressure in this module, but their explanations stayed structured and concise.
dimension_scores.evidence: They consistently explained what they tested, what it proved, and what was ruled out.

dimension_scores.observation: They went beyond surface symptoms and identified deeper causes, especially the difference between a misleading error and a process-lifecycle failure, and between offset math and consistency under concurrency.
dimension_scores.evidence: They explicitly distinguished the dead Uvicorn process from the redirect handler, and later explained why keyset pagination is a better structural fix than a tie-breaker alone.

dimension_scores.observation: Postmortem writing was not exercised yet in this module.
dimension_scores.evidence: The module focused on diagnosis and verification, not a retrospective writeup.

strengths: They consistently picked the cheapest discriminating test first, which is the core habit this module is trying to build.
They recognized when a symptom was misleading and adjusted their mental model instead of clinging to the first explanation.
growth_areas: They should build more comfort reading logs as a narrative once Module 2 starts, because that skill is still mostly untapped.
They have not yet practiced turning an incident into a formal, blameless writeup, so the reflection-to-postmortem step still needs work.
data.recommendation: Keep using the same pattern next module: write two falsifiable hypotheses before touching code, then force yourself to prove one wrong with the cheapest possible command.
